question.text: A pendulum of mass 1 kg and length $l=1 \mathrm{~m}$ is released from rest at angle $\theta=60^{\circ}$. The power delivered by all the forces acting on the bob at angle $\theta=30^{\circ}$ will be $\left(\right.$ Take, $\left.g=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2\right)$

solution.text: Power of tension $=0$ $\begin{aligned} & \text { Power of } m g=(m g)(v) \cos 60^{\circ} \\ & \text { Here, } \quad v=\sqrt{2 g h} \\ & \text { and } \quad h=l\left(\cos 30^{\circ}-\cos 60^{\circ}\right)=0.36 \mathrm{~m} \\ & v=\sqrt{2 \times 10 \times 0.36} \\ & =2.68 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s} \\ & \text { Power }=(m g)(v) \cos 60^{\circ} \\ & =(1 \times 10)(2.68) \times \frac{1}{2} \\ & =1.34 \times 10=13.4 \mathrm{~W} \end{aligned}$
